headline: NASA wants new astronauts to work on the Moon

sources.title: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon (NPR)
Nasa seeks next generation of astronauts to live and work on the moon (The Guardian)
NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps (NASA)

chunks.text: On Saturday, November 7, 2026, NASA {{kicked off}} a search for its next [[class]] of astronauts, a group that trains together. The U.S. [[space agency]] said the people it picks could walk on the Moon. They could also live and work at a planned Moon Base. The head of NASA said its astronauts have always been [[willing]] to {{take on}} very hard challenges. People can {{send in}} [[applications]] online until Thursday, December 3.

chunks.text: Applicants must be U.S. [[citizens]]. Most need a [[master's degree]] in science, technology, engineering or math. They also need three years of [[work experience]] in a [[related field]]. Doctors, people in a [[PhD program]] and pilots who have {{built up}} many [[flight hours]] can also apply. There is no official [[age limit]]. Before, nursing degrees were {{left out}} of NASA's list of science subjects. Now a master's in nursing counts too. This change {{opens the job up}} to nurses.

chunks.text: The job is very hard to get. When NASA last opened applications, in 2024, more than 8,000 {{poured in}}. The agency {{narrowed them down}} to just 10 new astronauts in 2025. Those 10 are still {{going through}} nearly two years of training. NASA has 32 [[active]] astronauts today. The [[starting salary]] for new astronauts is $164,395 a year.

verbs.wrong: To be refused without a reply
verbs.why: Letters pour in after a popular TV show. Calls pour in when a store has a big sale. When NASA last opened applications, in 2024, more than 8,000 poured in.

verbs.correct: To experience a long training process
verbs.wrong: To plan a training course for others
verbs.why: New nurses go through months of training. Every new worker goes through a safety course. The 10 astronauts chosen in 2025 are still going through nearly two years of training.

chunks.text: NASA plans to choose the new class in late 2027. Training lasts about two years and includes [[spacewalks]] and flying fast jets. The astronauts will get ready to {{carry out}} hard [[missions]], such as landing near the Moon's South Pole. NASA [[aims]] to return people to the Moon in 2028, for the first time since 1972. It has {{teamed up}} with [[private companies]] such as SpaceX to build the spacecraft. NASA's chief astronaut called the job a chance to help [[shape]] the future of people in space.

mainIdea.s: NASA has opened its search for a new group of astronauts who could live and work on the Moon. The job is hard to get, since only 10 people were picked from over 8,000 last time.
mainIdea.why: NASA kicked off a search for new astronauts who could live at a Moon Base. Last time, it narrowed more than 8,000 applications down to 10.

mainIdea.s: NASA is hiring a large team of space workers to build its Moon Base by 2028. Anyone can apply now, because the agency has dropped its rules about degrees and job history.
mainIdea.why: Close, but most applicants still need a master's degree and three years of work experience. Only the rule on nursing degrees changed.

mainIdea.s: Two American astronauts returned to Earth after a long stay on the space station. Doctors are now checking how many months without gravity changed their muscles and bones.
mainIdea.why: NASA kicked off a search for a new class of astronauts. The people it picks could one day walk on the Moon.

tf.s: NASA kicked off a search for a new class of astronauts.
tf.why: On November 7, 2026, NASA opened applications for its next group of astronauts.

tf.s: NASA says the people it picks will only work on Earth.
tf.why: They could walk on the Moon and live at a Moon Base. They will get ready to carry out hard missions there.

tf.s: NASA picked almost everyone who applied in its last call.
tf.why: More than 8,000 applications poured in, and NASA narrowed them down to just 10 people.

tf.s: Master's degrees in nursing are no longer left out.
tf.why: A master's in nursing now counts, which opens the job up to nurses.

tf.s: NASA has teamed up with private companies to build spacecraft.
tf.why: Companies such as SpaceX are building the spacecraft NASA needs to return people to the Moon.

tf.s: Applicants do not need any degree or work experience.
tf.why: Most need a master's degree and three years of work experience. Pilots who have built up many flight hours can also apply.

lines.text: Did you see that NASA {{kicked off}} a search for new astronauts?
I did. And this group could actually work on the Moon.
That's my [[dream job]]. Can anyone apply?
You have to be a U.S. citizen. Most people also need a master's degree and three years of work experience.
Pilots who have {{built up}} a lot of flight hours can apply too. And nursing degrees aren't {{left out}} anymore.
Nice. That {{opens it up}} to a lot of nurses.
It's very hard to get, though. Last time, more than 8,000 applications {{poured in}}.
Wow. How many people did they pick?
They {{narrowed them down}} to ten. Those ten are [[the cream of the crop]], and they're still {{going through}} their training.
Do you think you have [[the right stuff]]?
Maybe. The training lasts about two years. You study spacewalks and get ready to {{carry out}} hard missions.
Sounds like it's [[not for the faint of heart]].
It isn't. The head of NASA wants people who will {{take on}} very hard challenges.
Still, if you want to [[shoot for the moon]], this is the way to do it.
True. Just {{send in}} your application before December 3.
Will they really get to the Moon soon?
NASA aims to return people there in 2028. It has {{teamed up}} with private companies to build the spacecraft.
